title: ICSE | CLASS - 10 | chemistry Test | Matter | Physical &chemical changes | Elements, compounds & Mixtures | language of chemistry
description: ICSE | CLASS - 10 | chemistry Test | Matter | Physical &chemical changes | Elements, compounds & Mixtures | language of chemistry
subject: chemistry

questions.question: Which of the following statements is/are true regarding the intermolecular force of attraction in different states of matter? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is stronger in solids than in liquids.
It increases with an increase in temperature.

questions.explanation: Intermolecular force of attraction is strongest in solids, intermediate in liquids, and negligible in gases. Increasing temperature increases kinetic energy, which overcomes and weakens intermolecular forces.
questions.hint: Think about how closely packed particles are in solids versus gases.

questions.question: Which of the following substances undergo sublimation upon heating? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride, camphor, naphthalene, and iodine are sublimate substances that convert directly from solid to gaseous state without passing through the liquid state. Sodium chloride (table salt) melts at high temperatures.
questions.hint: These substances are often used as mothballs or in religious rituals and disappear over time without leaving liquid.

questions.question: What is the direct conversion of a gas into a solid without passing through the liquid state called?
questions.explanation: The direct transition of a substance from gas to solid is called deposition or desublimation. Sublimation is the reverse process (solid to gas).
questions.hint: This is the exact reverse of sublimation.

questions.question: Why do solids have a definite shape and a definite volume?

options.text: The particles have maximum kinetic energy.
The intermolecular spaces are minimum and intermolecular forces are maximum.
The particles can slide over one another easily.

questions.explanation: Due to maximum intermolecular forces and minimum intermolecular spaces, the particles in a solid are tightly locked in fixed positions, giving them a definite shape and volume.
questions.hint: Consider the strength of the forces holding the particles together in fixed positions.

questions.question: Which of the following phenomena demonstrate that particles of matter are continuously moving? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The spreading of fragrance from an incense stick across a room.
A drop of potassium permanganate turning a beaker of water purple over time.
A wooden block remaining stationary on a table.
The smell of hot cooked food reaching you from a distance.

questions.explanation: Diffusion (the intermixing of particles of two different types of matter on their own) occurs because particles possess kinetic energy and are in continuous random motion.
questions.hint: Look for examples where a substance spreads out spontaneously without stirring.

questions.question: During the boiling of water, what happens to the temperature of the water once it reaches 100°C under normal atmospheric pressure?

options.text: It continues to rise steadily until all water evaporates.
It remains constant until all the water converts into steam.
It decreases slightly due to energy loss.

questions.explanation: During boiling, the temperature remains constant at the boiling point (100°C for water) because the heat energy supplied is used up as latent heat of vaporization to break the intermolecular forces between water molecules.
questions.hint: Remember the concept of latent (hidden) heat during change of state.

questions.question: Which of the following statements correctly differentiates between evaporation and boiling? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Evaporation takes place at all temperatures, whereas boiling occurs at a specific temperature.
Evaporation is a surface phenomenon, whereas boiling is a bulk phenomenon.
Evaporation is a rapid process, whereas boiling is a slow process.
Evaporation causes cooling, whereas boiling does not cause cooling.

questions.explanation: Evaporation happens slowly at any temperature from the surface and causes cooling by absorbing high kinetic energy particles. Boiling occurs rapidly throughout the entire liquid volume only at the boiling point.
questions.hint: Think about drying clothes on a line versus heating water in a kettle on the stove.

questions.question: According to the kinetic molecular theory, what happens when a gas is compressed inside a cylinder?

options.text: The size of individual gas molecules decreases.
The mass of the gas molecules decreases.
The intermolecular spaces between the gas molecules decrease.
The kinetic energy of the molecules drops to zero immediately.

questions.explanation: Gases have large intermolecular spaces. When compressed under pressure, the molecules are pushed closer together, reducing the intermolecular space without changing the size or mass of the molecules themselves.
questions.hint: Compression affects the distance between particles, not the particles themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct ascending order of intermolecular spaces in different states of matter?
questions.explanation: Solids have the most tightly packed particles (minimum intermolecular space), liquids have slightly more space allowing them to flow, and gases have the maximum intermolecular space.
questions.hint: Ascending order means from smallest space to largest space.

questions.question: A sealed glass jar contains a gas. If the jar is heated, what physical changes occur at the molecular level? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The kinetic energy of the gas molecules increases.
The molecules strike the walls of the jar with greater frequency and force.
The actual volume of the glass jar shrinks significantly.

questions.explanation: Heating increases thermal energy, which converts into kinetic energy. The faster-moving gas molecules collide with the container walls more frequently and forcefully, increasing pressure.
questions.hint: Temperature is a direct measure of average kinetic energy.

questions.question: Which law states that matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction or physical change?
questions.explanation: The Law of Conservation of Mass, formulated by Antoine Lavoisier, states that the total mass of reactants equals the total mass of products in any physical or chemical change.
questions.hint: This foundational law ensures that the total mass before and after a change remains identical.

questions.question: Why does a gas completely fill the vessel in which it is kept?

options.text: Gas molecules have high density and settle at the bottom.
Gas molecules have negligible intermolecular attraction and high kinetic energy, moving randomly in all directions.
Gas molecules repel each other with extreme electromagnetic forces.
Gas molecules expand in volume to match the container size.

questions.explanation: Because intermolecular forces of attraction are negligible and kinetic energy is extremely high, gas particles move rapidly and randomly in all directions until they occupy all available space in the container.
questions.hint: Focus on the lack of holding forces and the high speed of gas particles.

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of chemical changes? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Rusting, curding, and digestion form entirely new substances with new chemical properties and are generally irreversible. Melting of ice is a physical change as no new substance is formed ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$ remains $\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
questions.hint: Look for processes where new substances with entirely different properties are permanently formed.

questions.question: Which of the following characteristics apply to a physical change? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It is generally temporary and reversible.
There is always a significant change in the total mass of the substance.
Only the physical properties like state, size, or shape change.

questions.explanation: In physical changes, the chemical composition remains identical, no new substances are produced, and the changes are typically reversible without any alteration in individual mass.
questions.hint: Think of cutting paper or freezing water-the composition stays the same.

questions.question: When baking soda is added to vinegar, a brisk effervescence is observed due to the evolution of a gas. What is the nature of this change and the identity of the gas?
questions.explanation: The reaction between baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) and vinegar (acetic acid) is a chemical change that produces new substances: sodium acetate, water, and carbon dioxide gas ($\text{CO}_2$), which causes effervescence.
questions.hint: This reaction creates a fizzing sound and releases the same gas we exhale during respiration.

questions.question: Which of the following processes are classified as exothermic changes? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Evaporation of water from a pond

questions.explanation: Exothermic changes release heat energy into the surroundings. Combustion, respiration, and the slaking of quicklime release significant amounts of heat. Evaporation absorbs heat (endothermic).
questions.hint: "Exo" means out or releasing; look for reactions that make the surroundings warmer.

questions.question: What are the essential conditions required for the rusting of iron to occur?

options.text: Presence of both oxygen (air) and moisture (water)

questions.explanation: Rusting is an oxidation process where iron reacts with oxygen in the presence of water/moisture to form hydrated iron(III) oxide ($\text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3 \cdot x\text{H}_2\text{O}$). Both air and moisture are strictly necessary.
questions.hint: Iron won't rust in boiled, oil-sealed water (no air) or in a desiccator with dry air (no moisture).

questions.question: Which common everyday event involves BOTH physical and chemical changes occurring simultaneously?

options.text: Tearing a piece of cloth into shreds

questions.explanation: When a candle burns, the melting of solid wax into liquid wax and vapor is a physical change (reversible). The burning of wax vapor to produce carbon dioxide, water vapor, heat, and light is a chemical change (irreversible).
questions.hint: Observe a lit candle: look at what happens to the wax structure versus the flame itself.

questions.question: Which of the following changes is an endothermic chemical change?
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis requires the absorption of solar energy (sunlight) to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen, making it an endothermic chemical change.
questions.hint: "Endo" means absorbing; think of a vital biological process that requires continuous sunlight to function.

questions.question: Why is the dissolution of sugar in water considered a physical change rather than a chemical change? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The sugar molecules retain their chemical identity and sweet taste.
The sugar can be recovered completely by physical methods like evaporation.
A new chemical substance called sugar-hydrate is formed.
No energy change of high magnitude occurs during the process.

questions.explanation: Dissolving sugar is physical because no new chemical bond is formed, properties remain unchanged, and the original sugar can be easily retrieved by evaporating the water.
questions.hint: Can you get the dry sugar crystals back just by boiling off the water?

questions.question: A student heats blue copper sulphate crystals ($\text{CuSO}_4 \cdot 5\text{H}_2\text{O}$) in a dry test tube. The crystals turn white, and water droplets condense on the cooler parts of the tube. When a few drops of water are added back to the white residue, it turns blue again. What type of change is this?
questions.explanation: Heating hydrated copper sulphate drives off the water of crystallization, leaving anhydrous white copper sulphate. Adding water reverses the process, restoring the blue color. Since it is reversible and no new substance is permanently formed, it is a physical change.
questions.hint: Notice that adding water restores the original substance and its color completely.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are true regarding the burning of a magnesium ribbon in air? (Select all that apply)

options.text: It burns with a dazzling white flame.
It is a chemical change resulting in the formation of basic magnesium oxide.
The white ash formed can be turned back into magnesium ribbon by physical cooling.

questions.explanation: Magnesium burns in oxygen with a bright white light, evolving heat (exothermic) and forming magnesium oxide ($\text{MgO}$ ash), which is a new chemical substance (chemical change). It cannot be reversed physically.
questions.hint: Think about laboratory demonstrations where metallic ribbon turns into white powder.

questions.question: What kind of change occurs when a piece of iron is magnetized using an electric current or a bar magnet?
questions.explanation: Magnetizing iron only temporarily aligns its magnetic domains. No new substance is formed, and the iron can easily lose its magnetism by hammering or heating, making it a reversible physical change.
questions.hint: Does the iron turn into a new chemical compound when it attracts paperclips?

questions.question: Which of the following represents an irreversible physical change?

options.text: Breaking a glass tumbler into pieces

questions.explanation: Breaking a glass tumbler is a physical change because the broken pieces are still glass (no new substance formed). However, you cannot easily reassemble the pieces back into the original tumbler shape, making it practically irreversible by simple physical means.
questions.hint: Look for an option where the material stays the same, but the shape cannot be undone.

questions.question: When green copper carbonate ($\text{CuCO}_3$) is heated strongly in a test tube, it decomposes to form a black residue of copper oxide ($\text{CuO}$) and releases carbon dioxide gas. How should this reaction be classified?
questions.explanation: Thermal decomposition requires continuous supply of heat (endothermic) and produces entirely new chemical substances ($\text{CuO}$ and $\text{CO}_2$) with properties different from green copper carbonate (chemical change).
questions.hint: Notice that continuous heat is required to break down one substance into two new different substances.

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) correctly describe(s) a chemical compound? (Select all that apply)

options.text: The elements in a compound are combined in a fixed ratio by mass.
A compound has properties entirely different from those of its constituent elements.
The components of a compound can be separated by simple physical methods like filtration.
The formation of a compound is usually accompanied by the absorption or evolution of energy.

questions.explanation: A compound is a pure substance made of two or more elements chemically combined in a fixed proportion by mass. Its properties differ from its constituents, and it can only be broken down by chemical or electrochemical methods.
questions.hint: Contrast how water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) behaves compared to elemental hydrogen and oxygen gases.

questions.question: Which of the following are characteristics of mixtures? (Select all that apply)

options.text: They can be homogeneous or heterogeneous.
The constituents retain their original chemical properties.
They always have a sharp and fixed melting or boiling point.
Their constituents can be mixed in any arbitrary proportion.

questions.explanation: Mixtures contain two or more substances physically mixed in any ratio without chemical bonding. They retain their individual properties, do not have sharp melting/boiling points, and can be separated physically.
questions.hint: Think of a fruit salad or saltwater-you can vary the recipe however you like.

questions.question: Which separation technique is best suited to separate a mixture of two immiscible liquids like oil and water?
questions.explanation: Immiscible liquids (like oil and water) form distinct layers based on their densities. A separating funnel allows the denser bottom layer (water) to be drained out separately from the lighter upper layer (oil).
questions.hint: This apparatus relies on difference in densities and lack of solubility between two liquids.

questions.question: Which of the following substances are classified as pure substances? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Pure substances consist of only one type of particle (either a single element like gold, or a single chemical compound like water and sodium chloride). Air is a homogeneous mixture of various gases.
questions.hint: Check if the substance can be represented by a single chemical formula or symbol.

questions.question: A mixture contains common salt ($\text{NaCl}$) and ammonium chloride ($\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$). Which physical method should be used to separate ammonium chloride from the mixture?
questions.explanation: Ammonium chloride is a sublimate (it converts directly from solid to vapor when heated), whereas common salt is non-sublimable. Heating the mixture vaporizes the ammonium chloride, which condenses on a cool surface, leaving common salt behind.
questions.hint: Identify which of the two salts turns directly into a gas upon heating.

questions.question: What is the underlying principle behind paper chromatography used for separating colored components of ink?

options.text: Difference in boiling points of the components
Difference in solubility of the components in the same solvent
Difference in magnetic properties of the dyes
Difference in particle size during filtration

questions.explanation: Chromatography separates dyes based on their different rates of solubility and adsorption in a moving liquid solvent across a stationary phase (filter paper). More soluble dyes travel faster and higher up the paper.
questions.hint: Think about how different colors spread out at different speeds when water touches an ink dot on paper.

questions.question: Suppose you are given a dry powder mixture containing iron filings, sulphur powder, and common salt. Which sequence of methods is correct to separate all three components individually? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Use a magnet to remove iron filings -> Add water to dissolve salt -> Filter out insoluble sulphur -> Evaporate filtrate to get salt.
Add carbon disulphide ($\text{CS}_2$) to dissolve sulphur and filter it out -> Use a magnet on the residue to separate iron from salt.
Sublime the mixture to remove salt -> Use a magnet to remove sulphur from iron.
Distill the dry powder directly at 100°C.

questions.explanation: Iron is magnetic; sulphur is soluble in carbon disulphide ($\text{CS}_2$) but insoluble in water; salt is soluble in water but insoluble in $\text{CS}_2$. Using magnetism, selective dissolution, filtration, and evaporation separates all components cleanly.
questions.hint: Exploit the unique physical property of each item: magnetism for iron, water-solubility for salt, or $\text{CS}_2$-solubility for sulphur.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a heterogeneous mixture?

options.text: A mixture of sand and water

questions.explanation: A heterogeneous mixture does not have a uniform composition throughout, and its boundary of separation between components is visible (like sand settling in water). Alloys, true solutions, and clean air are homogeneous.
questions.hint: Look for an option where you can clearly see different physical phases or layers with your naked eye.

questions.question: How does a heated, chemically combined compound of iron and sulphur (Iron(II) sulphide, $\text{FeS}$) behave differently from a simple physical mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder? (Select all that apply)

options.text: $\text{FeS}$ is not attracted by a magnet, whereas iron in the mixture is attracted.
When dilute hydrochloric acid is added to $\text{FeS}$, foul-smelling hydrogen sulphide ($\text{H}_2\text{S}$) gas is evolved.
Sulphur cannot be dissolved out of $\text{FeS}$ using carbon disulphide solvent.
The compound $\text{FeS}$ retains the bright yellow color of pure sulphur.

questions.explanation: In $\text{FeS}$, iron and sulphur lose their individual chemical and physical properties. It is non-magnetic, insoluble in $\text{CS}_2$, and reacts with acids to produce rotten-egg smelling $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ gas rather than hydrogen gas.
questions.hint: Once elements chemically combine into a compound, they lose their original identity completely.

questions.question: Why is water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) considered a compound and not a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Hydrogen and oxygen are combined in a fixed ratio of 1:8 by mass.
Water is a liquid that extinguishes fire, whereas hydrogen is combustible and oxygen supports combustion.
Its constituents cannot be separated by physical methods like boiling or filtration.
Water has a variable boiling point depending on how it was prepared.

questions.explanation: Water has a fixed composition by mass (1:8), a sharp boiling point (100°C), and properties completely opposite to its constituent gases. It can only be separated chemically via electrolysis.
questions.hint: Can you separate hydrogen and oxygen gas from pure water just by filtering or spinning it?

questions.question: What type of mixture is an alloy such as stainless steel or bronze?
questions.explanation: An alloy is a uniform, homogeneous mixture of two or more metals (or a metal and a non-metal) mixed together in the molten state and solidified, showing uniform properties throughout.
questions.hint: Think of metal mixtures where you cannot see the distinct constituent metals separated from one another.

questions.question: Which technique is used to separate two miscible liquids having a difference in their boiling points of less than 25°C (like acetone and methanol)?
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation uses a fractionating column that provides repeated condensation and vaporization surfaces, allowing clean separation of miscible liquids with close boiling points (<25°C difference).
questions.hint: This advanced distillation method uses glass beads or a specialized column to separate close-boiling liquids like crude oil components.

questions.question: Which of the following elements are correctly matched with their Latin names from which their chemical symbols are derived? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Many symbols come from Latin names: Natrium ($\text{Na}$ for Sodium), Kalium ($\text{K}$ for Potassium), Ferrum ($\text{Fe}$ for Iron), Cuprum ($\text{Cu}$ for Copper), Argentum ($\text{Ag}$ for Silver), and Aurum ($\text{Au}$ for Gold).
questions.hint: Think about why Sodium uses 'Na' instead of 'So' or 'S'.

questions.question: What is the valency of the phosphate radical ($\text{PO}_4$) and what formula does it form when combined with calcium ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$)?
questions.explanation: The phosphate radical is trivalent ($\text{PO}_4^{3-}$). Calcium is divalent ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$). Applying the criss-cross method of valencies gives the formula $\text{Ca}_3(\text{PO}_4)_2$.
questions.hint: Criss-cross the charges: swap the 2 from Calcium and the 3 from Phosphate.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct chemical formula for Aluminum Sulphate?
questions.explanation: Aluminum has a valency of 3+ ($\text{Al}^{3+}$) and the sulphate radical has a valency of 2- ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$). Criss-crossing these valencies yields $\text{Al}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$.
questions.hint: Aluminum is in Group 13 (valency 3) and Sulphate has a charge of -2.

questions.question: Which of the following basic radicals exhibit a divalent (+2) charge? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Ferrous (Iron-II), Cupric (Copper-II), Magnesium, Calcium, and Zinc are divalent electropositive (basic) radicals with a +2 charge. Ferric is trivalent (+3).
questions.hint: Look for the "-ous" or "-ic" endings: "Ferrous" is lower valency (+2), while "Ferric" is higher (+3).

questions.question: In the balanced chemical equation for the synthesis of ammonia: $x\text{N}_2 + y\text{H}_2 \rightarrow z\text{NH}_3$, what are the correct integer coefficients for $x$, $y$, and $z$?
questions.explanation: To balance nitrogen atoms, $z$ must be 2 when $x=1$ ($1\text{N}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3$). This gives 6 hydrogen atoms on the right, requiring $y=3$ ($3\text{H}_2$) on the left. Thus, the balanced equation is $\text{N}_2 + 3\text{H}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{NH}_3$.
questions.hint: Make sure the total count of Nitrogen atoms and Hydrogen atoms is identical on both sides of the arrow.

questions.question: Which of the following transition metals exhibit variable valency in their compounds? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Transition metals like Iron (+2, +3), Copper (+1, +2), and Mercury (+1, +2) exhibit variable valencies due to the availability of inner shell electrons for bonding. Group 1 alkali metals like Sodium strictly show a valency of +1.
questions.hint: Which of these metals have both "-ous" and "-ic" compound names (like Cuprous/Cupric)?

questions.question: Which of the following polyatomic radicals are electronegative acid radicals with a monovalent (-1) charge? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Nitrate, bicarbonate, hydroxide, and chloride are monovalent acid radicals (-1 charge). Carbonate ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) and Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) are divalent (-2 charge).
questions.hint: Check which radicals require only one Sodium ion ($\text{Na}^+$) to form a neutral compound.

questions.question: What is the atomicity of a molecule of Sulphur (in standard solid state) and Phosphorus (in vapor state), respectively?
questions.explanation: Solid sulphur exists as polyatomic octatomic molecules ($\text{S}_8$, atomicity = 8). Phosphorus vapor exists as tetratomic molecules ($\text{P}_4$, atomicity = 4).
questions.hint: Atomicity is the total number of atoms present in one molecule of an element.

questions.question: Which of the following chemical formulas are correctly written according to the rules of valency? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: $\text{Mg}^{2+}$ and $\text{N}^{3-}$ criss-cross to form $\text{Mg}_3\text{N}_2$. $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ form $(\text{NH}_4)_2\text{CO}_3$. Potassium ($\text{K}^+$) and Dichromate ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) form $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$. Calcium hydroxide must have brackets around hydroxide: $\text{Ca}(\text{OH})_2$.
questions.hint: Always use parentheses around polyatomic radicals when their subscript is greater than 1.

questions.question: Why is it mandatory to balance a chemical equation?

options.text: To ensure the number of molecules remains constant.
To satisfy the Law of Conservation of Mass.
To prevent the reactants from evaporating.

questions.explanation: According to the Law of Conservation of Mass, matter can neither be created nor destroyed. Therefore, the total number of atoms of each element must be equal on both reactant and product sides of a chemical equation.
questions.hint: Think about Lavoisier's rule: total mass before reaction must equal total mass after reaction.

questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name for the compound $\text{P}_2\text{O}_5$?
questions.explanation: For binary compounds of two non-metals, Greek prefixes are used to specify the number of atoms: "di-" for 2 phosphorus atoms and "penta-" for 5 oxygen atoms, forming Diphosphorus pentoxide.
questions.hint: Notice the subscripts 2 and 5: use "di" for two and "penta" for five.

questions.question: Consider the reaction of lead(II) nitrate decomposition upon heating: $2\text{Pb}(\text{NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{PbO} + x\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$. What is the value of $x$ to balance the equation?
questions.explanation: On the reactant side, there are $2 \times 2 = 4$ nitrogen atoms and $2 \times 6 = 12$ oxygen atoms. To balance nitrogen on the product side, $x$ must be 4 ($4\text{NO}_2$). Let's check oxygen: $2(\text{in PbO}) + 8(\text{in } 4\text{NO}_2) + 2(\text{in O}_2) = 12$ oxygen atoms. Thus, $x = 4$.
questions.hint: Count the total number of Nitrogen (N) atoms on the left side of the arrow first.

questions.question: A metal $\text{M}$ forms a chloride with the formula $\text{MCl}_3$. What will be the formula of its oxide and sulphate, respectively?
questions.explanation: Since chlorine has a valency of -1 ($\text{Cl}^-$), the formula $\text{MCl}_3$ shows that metal $\text{M}$ has a valency of +3 ($\text{M}^{3+}$). Combining $\text{M}^{3+}$ with Oxide ($\text{O}^{2-}$) gives $\text{M}_2\text{O}_3$. Combining $\text{M}^{3+}$ with Sulphate ($\text{SO}_4^{2-}$) gives $\text{M}_2(\text{SO}_4)_3$.
questions.hint: First deduce the valency of metal M from the chloride formula, then criss-cross that valency with Oxide (-2) and Sulphate (-2).
